summary: Bink video frame decoder (thiscall). Waits for the next frame (BinkWait on the Bink handle at this+0), decompresses it with BinkDoFrame, advances with BinkNextFrame, and wraps the frame index this[1] modulo the total frame count read from the Bink header at *this+8. Then maps the render-path flag a2[12] through a jump table into a copy-flag word, ORs high bits from the a5 flags (0x20 sets 0x80000000, 0x10 sets 0x60000000), locks a surface via ThunkWithArgReorder, copies the frame with BinkCopyToBuffer, clears bit 0x400 of a2[6], and returns the surface-unlock result.

local_names.v6: copy-flag word assembled from the a2[12] switch, the a5 bits and the a2 pointer default
local_names.result: return of the surface unlock/return helper

operations.description: Advance the frame only when BinkWait(*this) returns 0 (next frame is ready); otherwise skip the frame-advance block.
BinkDoFrame(*this) decompresses and renders the current frame.
BinkNextFrame(*this) advances the Bink stream to the next frame.
Advance and wrap the current frame index: this[1] = (this[1] + 1) % *(int*)(*this + 8), using the total frame count read from the Bink header.
Select the base copy-flag value v6 from the render-path flag a2[12] via the jump table: case 5 -> 9, case 6 -> 10, case 7 -> 1, case 8 -> 5, default keeps the a2 pointer value.
OR the high flag bits into v6 from a5: when (a5 & 0x20) != 0 set 0x80000000; when (a5 & 0x10) != 0 set 0x60000000.
ThunkWithArgReorder(a2, 4, 0) locks the surface/buffer and returns a destination pointer as result.
When a surface was obtained, BinkCopyToBuffer(*this, result, a2[10], a2[8], a3, a4, v6) copies the decoded frame into the buffer using the surface pitch, rect and assembled flags.
ArgumentReorderWrapper_3230(a2, 4, 0) unlocks/releases the surface; result takes its return value.
Clear bit 0x400 of a2[6] after the copy.
